description:
## What the code does

Within crate-jmap-calendars-client, two modules import `CALL_ID` and the relevant `USING_*` constant into local scope at the top of the file:

```rust
// crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/event_parse.rs:5
use super::{CalendarEventParseResponse, SessionClient, CALL_ID, USING_PARSE};

// crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/principal_availability.rs:5
use super::{PrincipalGetAvailabilityResponse, SessionClient, CALL_ID, USING_AVAILABILITY};
```

Then reference them unqualified: `build_request(..., USING_PARSE)`, `extract_response(&resp, CALL_ID)`.

The other four method modules in the same crate (`calendar.rs`, `event.rs`, `event_notification.rs`, `participant_identity.rs`) do NOT import these constants — they use `super::CALL_ID` and `super::USING_CALENDARS` qualifications at each call site:

```rust
// crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/calendar.rs:43-45
let req = super::build_request("Calendar/get", args, super::USING_CALENDARS);
let resp = self.call_internal(api_url, &req).await?;
jmap_base_client::extract_response(&resp, super::CALL_ID)
```

## What idiomatic Rust would do

Pick one style and use it consistently within a crate. The canonical `crate-jmap-mail-client/src/methods/email.rs` uses the qualified `super::CALL_ID` / `super::USING_MAIL` style throughout — see lines 61, 63, 89, 91, 131, 133, 168, 170, 198, 200, 225, 227, 280, 282, 326, 328. No method module in canonical mail-client imports `CALL_ID`.

## Why it matters

This is the lowest-stakes complaint in this pass — there is no engineering harm; both styles compile, both produce identical code. But:

1. **Cookie-cutter consistency.** Per workspace AGENTS.md, calendars-client should mirror the canonical pattern. `event_parse.rs` and `principal_availability.rs` are the outliers.

2. **Internal consistency within calendars-client itself.** Four files use one style, two use the other. A drive-by contributor adding a method to this crate has to pick one style based on which file they happened to copy from. The two are not even split by method shape — `event_parse` and `principal_availability` are both methods that need a non-default `USING_*` constant. That is a real semantic distinction the import style could be tracking ("non-standard capability set: imported; standard: qualified"), but no docstring or comment explains the convention either way, so the consistent reading is "unintentional drift".

## Fix shape

Remove the `CALL_ID, USING_*` imports from `event_parse.rs:5` and `principal_availability.rs:5`. Replace the unqualified references inside each method body with `super::CALL_ID` and `super::USING_PARSE` / `super::USING_AVAILABILITY`. Mechanical, three sites per file.

## Source citations

- crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/event_parse.rs:5, 35, 37
- crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/principal_availability.rs:5, 41, 43
- crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/calendar.rs:43-45 (qualified style, in-crate)
- crate-jmap-mail-client/src/methods/email.rs:61-63 (qualified style, canonical)
title: Internal import-style inconsistency: event_parse/principal_availability use `CALL_ID` / `USING_*` directly while other modules use `super::` prefix
